description:
## Hypothesis

This crate is the wire-format deserialize boundary for RFC 9610 Contacts. Every `pub struct` here derives `Deserialize` and is called via `serde_json::from_str`/`from_value` on bytes that originate from an untrusted JMAP client. The existing test suite covers happy paths and a handful of edge cases (null `shareWith`, false-valued booleans in MUST-true maps, slash-keyed filter fields). It does **not** exercise:

- Malformed JSON (truncated objects, mismatched braces, invalid UTF-8 escapes)
- Oversized strings (e.g. `name` field exceeding the RFC 9610 §2 documented 255 UTF-8 octet bound)
- Integer overflow (e.g. `sortOrder` >= 2^31 — spec range is `[0, 2^31)`; type is `u32` allowing up to 2^32-1, so values in [2^31, 2^32) deserialise as valid `u32` but are wire-protocol violations)
- Non-object values where the wire shape expects an object (e.g. `name: "vincent"` instead of `name: {...}` — the Sloppy-Value fields accept ANY JSON, see card.rs lines 124-137)
- Deeply-nested sloppy fields (e.g. `{"name":{"a":{"a":{...}}}\}` — `serde_json`'s default recursion limit of 128 protects against unbounded stack but does not bound memory)
- Duplicate JSON object keys (RFC 8259 §4 leaves behavior implementation-defined; `serde_json` last-wins)

## What goes wrong without negative tests

A type crate that ships without negative tests provides no contract to downstream consumers about what malformed input does. Three concrete risks:

1. **Integrity**: a server that trusts `sortOrder: 2147483648` round-trips through this type cleanly and ends up storing a wire-protocol violation. JMAP-glx8 line-of-defense was 'handler layer rejects', but the handler crate doesn't exist yet (jmap-contacts-server is bd:JMAP-yfpq) and a downstream consumer reading this crate's docs has no test to point at confirming the type accepts the invalid value cleanly.
2. **DoS**: per the workspace test-integrity rule, a passing test suite that doesn't exercise oversized/malformed input means a future refactor could break input-handling silently. No regression net.
3. **Spec-conformance proof**: every deserialise test should have a paired negative test demonstrating the type rejects-or-cleanly-accepts wire violations. Acceptance criteria below pin the exact shape.

## Acceptance criteria

Add tests under `tests::negative_deserialise` covering, at minimum:

1. `malformed_json_returns_error` — truncated object, mismatched brace, unterminated string each produce `Err` from `from_str`, not panic.
2. `oversized_name_deserialises_to_typed_field` — a 1000-byte name string deserialises cleanly (the 255-octet bound is handler-layer territory) and the test documents that fact.
3. `sort_order_overflow_outside_spec_range_accepts` — values in `[2^31, 2^32)` deserialise to typed `u32` without error; documents the spec-range vs type-range gap.
4. `sloppy_field_accepts_non_object_value` — `{ "name": "vincent" }` deserialises cleanly into `Option<serde_json::Value>` (the Sloppy-Value contract); `serde_json::from_value::<Name>(card.name.unwrap())` then returns `Err`. Documents handler-layer responsibility.
5. `deeply_nested_sloppy_field_within_serde_json_limit_succeeds` — 100-deep nested object deserialises cleanly.
6. `deeply_nested_sloppy_field_beyond_serde_json_limit_errors` — 200-deep nested object returns `Err` from `serde_json` (default RECURSION_LIMIT is 128).
7. `duplicate_keys_last_wins` — JSON object with two `"id"` keys serialises the second value; documents the duplicate-key contract referenced in card.rs:247-267.

Each test asserts ONLY the documented behavior of the type (cleanly-accepts or returns-Err); none assert handler-layer rejection (out of scope for a type crate).

## Probe / downstream session

A downstream `/do-beads JMAP-glx8` session executes the bead under appropriate permissions:

1. Read card.rs:124-137 (Sloppy-Value contract) and lines 247-267 (extras collision contract).
2. Add the 7 tests above to `src/lib.rs` tests module, following the existing oracle convention (Oracle: hand-typed JSON modelling the malformed shape).
3. Run `cargo test -p jmap-contacts-types` to verify all pass.

No existing test or library code is changed; only new tests are added. Out-of-scope per workspace convention: changing the `u32` to a bounded type to enforce the spec range, adding length validation to the type. Those are handler-layer concerns.

## Cross-reference

- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Test Integrity' — negative tests use independent oracles.
- card.rs:124-137 — Sloppy-Value contract that this test pins.
- card.rs:247-267 — extras collision contract that test 7 pins.
- bd:JMAP-yfpq — jmap-contacts-server (handler layer that will own pre-deserialise validation).
title: No negative-deserialization tests at the wire boundary (malformed/oversized/overflow input)
